title: GPT 5.6 - Who Has Tried It Yet?
author: bingewavecinema
selftext: Is it good at coding games? Or like all new models at first. hallucinates?

comments.author: Specific-Animal6570
comments.body:
Very fast & token efficient. 

But it makes small mistakes that it shouldn't make. I'm talking about the cheapest model on XHigh.

yes, really good. 

Fable level for what i can see

replies.body: Really? Are you not using the ultra? Because thats not what I’m hearing

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: my understanding is ultra is the setting that allows it to divide tasks and give them to other agents.  which can then be terra or even luna models.

replies.author: Kingnorik
replies.body: Old Fable or new Fable? New Fable is barely better than 5.5 for me.

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body: It really isn't. It only falls back to Opus on certain tasks. But I can tell you for a fact that Fable right now still breezes through issues that Opus takes several tilts to solve.

comments.author: HaMMeReD
comments.body:
I have it running on some tasks, some shader optimizations of my lbm/fluid system.

It hasn't broken anything yet. To soon to really know but it looks promising. It's challenging work and it's going in the right direction.

comments.author: Godszgift
comments.body: its amazing defintely fable level. i love it

comments.author: Ok_Sheepherder_5552
comments.body: It'd be interesting to see what you've made. I was trying Grok 4.5, and it's quite decent for prototyping games. I'll come back to report on GPT 5.6 tomorrow or so.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: from what I can tell, the new grok is good if you want to iterate fast and cheap.  Fable and Sol are if you want to just unleash the AI, and dont mind it costing a lot.

comments.author: Strict_Blacksmith462
comments.body: I’ve only tested it briefly so far. It feels stronger at following complex instructions and keeping context, but I’m still curious whether the improvement is noticeable in everyday coding and research tasks.

comments.author: GlitteringJob9248
comments.body: Not as creative as fable but was okay. Good at engineering

comments.author: Glitchy-stitchy
comments.body: It’s the equivalent of asking Jeeves a question while eating drywall. So what if it’s fast. i know I can’t read an Olympic level rates. Hasn’t a hint of personality. Might as well talk to a toaster.

comments.author: Technical-County-727
comments.body: Can’t compare to fable, but against 5.5, it is really really good

comments.author: Tough-Requirement707
comments.body: for game coding its far worse than 5.5 or opus 4.8 - 5.5 didnt make any mistake at all the last few weeks in my workflows, only something forgotten from time to time that was fixed with a follow up. 5.6sol on the other hand does the old shit again with regression introducing, doing the complete opposite of what was prompted which is the most cancer shit ever that can happen. i tried several different things and it always did that same degrading fuck ups no matter what section of the backend and on ui edits its even worse. i dont understand how that is supposed to be bettter?

comments.author: thatkidnamedrocky
comments.body: Nice upgrade, deepseek flash has been my main workhorse but I’m thinking I might stick with Luna High moving forward

comments.author: OldManActual
comments.body:
I used 5.6 Ultra today. I had a very slow report with a data table of over a million rows. I have spent a month with 5.5 trying to optimize it and 5.6 did the job in 40 minutes with one prompt in Codex. 

It was my first “one shot” on a real job. It wrote about ten scripts and I have all the intermediate products and an optimization report. 

It’s a leap but very expensive at the moment. Super impressed.
